title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
text:
These short activities show how AI assistants can help with common tasks: understanding documents, checking forms, drafting emails, processing notes and planning activities. We are using UU AI-Chat as the university’s approved platform.

Open UU AI-Chat and sign in with your UU account.
Use the Contents sidebar to choose an activity. Exercises start collapsed. Select one from the sidebar or click its title to expand it.
Open or download the linked fictional material, then paste its text or upload the file where supported. Copy the suggested prompt into UU AI-Chat and inspect the result.

Optional introductory slides
All training documents are fictional, not official Utrecht University rules or forms. Do not upload real confidential, personal, or sensitive records without the necessary permission and data-protection checks. Check AI responses against the original sources before using them.

title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
text:
Exercise 1: Decode instructions






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. You have a procedure describing which expenses can be reimbursed after attending a work event. You want to know what to do without reading the entire guide repeatedly.
Attach: 01_simulated_reimbursement_guide.md.
Try this prompt:
Explain the attached reimbursement guide to a colleague who has just attended a one-day work event.

Give me a short checklist: what can be claimed, which approvals and receipts are needed, and when the claim is due. Point to the relevant sections of the guide. If the guide does not answer something, say so rather than guessing.
Then try: Ask, “Can I claim a taxi without prior approval if it was more convenient?”
Check: Did the answer accurately capture exceptions, documentation and deadlines? Can you find each important rule in the original file?

title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
text:
Exercise 2: Review a completed form






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. A draft reimbursement claim needs a second check before submission. The draft deliberately contains several mistakes and missing details.
Attach: 01_simulated_reimbursement_guide.md and 02_simulated_completed_claim.md.
Try this prompt:
Review the attached completed claim against the attached reimbursement guide.

List possible mistakes or missing information in a table with: item, problem, relevant rule, and suggested next step. Check the arithmetic. Distinguish clear mismatches from points that need clarification. Do not assume that missing approvals exist or that the claim has been approved.
Then try: Ask which entries appear to comply with the guide, not just which ones are problematic.
Check: Did it catch the deliberate issues without inventing additional requirements? Did it distinguish a definite error from an open question? Review the findings before deciding what to change or submit.
Want to reuse this? Try Exercise 12 to configure a form-reviewing Persona and test it on a different claim.

title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
section: Exercise 3: Draft or improve an email
text:
Exercise 3: Draft or improve an email






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. You need to invite colleagues to a welcome session. You have rough notes but no finished message.
Your notes:

Welcome session: Wednesday 9 December 2026, 10:00–11:30.
Purpose: introduce new colleagues to the department’s support teams.
Room is not yet confirmed.
Ask people to register by 1 December using [registration link].
Tone: professional, friendly and concise.

Try this prompt:
Turn the notes below into a short, friendly email inviting colleagues to a welcome session.

Include a subject line, make the registration deadline clear, and keep [registration link] as a placeholder. Do not invent a room or other missing details.

Notes:
[PASTE THE NOTES ABOVE]
Then try: Ask for a shorter version for an intranet announcement, or a more formal version for external guests.
Check: Did it preserve all dates and avoid making up a venue? Is the tone appropriate for the recipients?
Want to reuse this? Try Exercise 11 to save the reusable writing instructions, without saving this event’s details.

title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
text:
Exercise 4: Process meeting notes






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. You have rough notes from a planning meeting and need to identify decisions and next steps.
Attach: 03_simulated_meeting_notes.md.
Try this prompt:
Turn these meeting notes into a concise follow-up summary.

Separate confirmed decisions, action items (with owners and deadlines where stated), proposals that are not yet agreed, and unresolved questions. Do not invent responsibilities or turn suggestions into decisions.
Then try: Ask for a short follow-up email to the attendees based on the same notes.
Check: Did it correctly distinguish confirmed arrangements from tentative suggestions? Are owners and deadlines supported by the notes?

title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
section: Exercise 5: Compare two versions of a procedure
text:
Exercise 5: Compare two versions of a procedure






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. A room-booking procedure has been updated. You want to know what changed and which version applies.
Attach: 04_room_booking_procedure_v1.md and 05_room_booking_procedure_v2.md.
Try this prompt:
Compare the two attached versions of the room-booking procedure.

Make a short table showing the substantive changes, including deadlines and accessibility arrangements. Explain when each version applies. Keep the explanation grounded in the documents, and note which rules have not changed.
Then try: Ask which version applies to a request submitted on 28 October 2026 for an event taking place on 20 November 2026.
Check: Did it notice the transition rule and avoid assuming the event date alone determines which version applies?

title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
section: Exercise 6: Turn a procedure into an FAQ
text:
Exercise 6: Turn a procedure into an FAQ






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. Colleagues keep asking the same questions about booking rooms, equipment and catering.
Attach: 05_room_booking_procedure_v2.md.
Try this prompt:
Create a short FAQ for colleagues booking an event, based only on the attached procedure.

Include questions about room booking, hybrid/AV support, catering, accessibility and cancellations. Use plain language and refer to the source section for each answer. Mark anything the document does not specify instead of filling in the gaps.
Then try: Ask for a one-page checklist instead of an FAQ.
Check: Did it capture working-day deadlines accurately? Did it add rules that were not in the document?

section: Exercise 7: Translate and simplify a message
text:
Exercise 7: Translate and simplify a message






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. You are preparing an English version of a Dutch announcement for international colleagues.
Attach: 07_simulated_dutch_announcement.md.
Try this prompt:
Translate the attached Dutch announcement into clear, natural English for international colleagues.

Keep the dates, registration deadline, and distinction between confirmed and unconfirmed details exactly as in the original. Use clear, professional language without adding new information.
Then try: Ask for a shorter version suitable for a newsletter or a plain-Dutch rewrite of the original.
Check: Did it preserve what is still uncertain? Would a colleague be able to act on the translated message?

title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
text:
Exercise 8: Plan an event






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. You have an initial event brief, but the organisers still need a practical plan.
Attach: 06_simulated_event_brief.md.
Try this prompt:
Turn the attached event brief into a practical preparation checklist.

Group tasks into what is already assigned, what still needs an owner, and decisions that are still open. Include stated deadlines and flag dependencies (for example, what must happen before invitations can be sent). Do not assume that rooms, spending or hybrid arrangements have been approved.
Then try: Ask for a draft agenda that fits the event objectives and duration, clearly labelled as a proposal.
Check: Did it preserve the difference between known facts, suggestions and unconfirmed arrangements?
Want to reuse this? Try Exercise 13 to create an event Project and update the plan across two chats.

title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
text:
Exercise 9: Check a simple spreadsheet






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. You have a small list of purchases for an event and want to check the calculations.
Attach: 08_simulated_purchases.csv.
Try this prompt:
Check the attached purchase list. For each row, compare quantity × unit price with the reported total.

Identify discrepancies in a small table, show the correct calculations, and explain how I could do this check with an Excel formula. Do not silently correct the source data. Summarise the total difference, if any.
Then try: Ask which items contribute most to the total estimated cost, or ask for a formula to calculate the total by category.
Check: Did it identify the right rows and calculate accurately? Can you verify a couple of items yourself with a calculator?

title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
text:
Exercise 10: Bring your own task






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. You have a recurring task that is not covered by the examples.
Choose a real type of task, but use fictional or approved non-sensitive example content. For example: rewriting reminders, summarising guidance, making a checklist or checking the structure of a form.
Prompt starter:
I often need to [DESCRIBE A ROUTINE TASK]. Here is a fictional example of the information I work with: [EXAMPLE].

Help me produce [DESIRED OUTPUT]. Keep these constraints in mind: [IMPORTANT RULES OR STYLE]. If essential information is missing, ask me rather than guessing.
Check: Would the reviewed output save time? Which parts would still need a person to decide or verify?

title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
section: Exercise 11: Save a Prompt for repeated emails
text:
Exercise 11: Save a Prompt for repeated emails






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. You often turn rough notes into emails. Save the recurring instructions under Prompts instead of typing them each time.
Try this: Open Prompts in UU AI-Chat, add a new prompt, and name it Staff email from rough notes. Save only the reusable instructions below. Leave out details specific to one event.
Turn the notes below into a short, clear email for colleagues.

Include a subject line. Preserve names, dates, and deadlines. Use a professional, friendly tone. Do not invent missing details. Flag anything that needs clarification.

Notes:
[PASTE NEW NOTES HERE]
Test it: Insert the saved Prompt into a new chat, replacing the placeholder with these different notes:

Office-hour change: from 7 December, walk-in support is on Tuesdays from 14:00 to 15:00 instead of 13:00 to 14:00. This arrangement ends after 19 December. Room B.14 is unchanged. Direct questions to [contact].

Check: Did the saved instructions work with the new information? Did the model retain the temporary dates, old/new time and contact placeholder? How would you improve the saved wording?

title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
section: Exercise 12: Build a reusable form-reviewer Persona
text:
Exercise 12: Build a reusable form-reviewer Persona






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. If you review forms regularly, a Persona can reuse the same instructions for each new form.
Use: 01_simulated_reimbursement_guide.md, 02_simulated_completed_claim.md, and 09_simulated_second_claim.md.

If you have not done Exercise 2, first attach the guide and first claim to a normal chat and request a check using the Exercise 2 prompt.
Open Personas and create a Persona named Expense claim reviewer. Give it the instructions below. If the Persona editor supports Sources/reference documents, attach the fictional reimbursement guide there. Otherwise attach the guide whenever you use the Persona.
Open a new chat using the Persona and attach 09_simulated_second_claim.md (and the guide if it is not attached to the Persona).
Ask: Review this draft claim against the reimbursement guide. What requires attention, and what appears compliant?

Persona instructions (save these as the Persona’s working method, not as a one-time chat message):
Review draft expense claims against a supplied procedure.

Check required fields, supporting receipts, approvals, deadlines, expense limits and arithmetic. For possible problems, cite the relevant rule and the form entry. Separate confirmed mismatches from missing documentation or uncertainty.

Use only the supplied guide as the authority. Do not invent requirements, approve claims or submit anything. End with a short list of issues for a person to review.
Check: Does the Persona identify the new claim’s issues without carrying over problems unique to the first claim? Can it show which rules support its findings? Would a saved Prompt be sufficient here, or does the Persona offer a useful advantage?
If source attachment or Persona settings differ in UU AI-Chat, keep the instructions in the Persona and attach the guide within the chat. The aim is to test reusable instructions, not a particular settings panel.

title: AI assistants for everyday tasks
section: Exercise 13: Use a Project across separate chats
text:
Exercise 13: Use a Project across separate chats






NoteOpen exercise





Scenario. An event may require several conversations. A Project keeps related documents, decisions and chats together.
Use: 06_simulated_event_brief.md and 10_simulated_event_status_update.md.

Open Projects, create Interdisciplinary Staff Afternoon, and add the two fictional files to the Project (not just a single chat).
If the Project supports instructions, add: For this event, distinguish confirmed decisions, proposals and missing information. Treat the latest dated update as more recent than the original brief. Never claim a booking or invitation has been completed unless a document says so.
In Chat 1, ask: From the event brief, what needs doing, who owns it, and what is undecided?
In Chat 2, ask: Using the event brief and the latest status update in this Project, draft a concise status email for the organisers. What changed, and what is still open?

Check: Did Chat 2 take account of the updated decisions without losing the original event’s objectives or constraints? Did it distinguish a room being available from booked? Did it avoid treating a proposed registration deadline as agreed?
Note: Shared Project context may not be applied consistently across chats. If a detail is missing or wrong, refer the AI explicitly to the relevant project file or save a key decision in project knowledge (where available), then verify the answer again.
